title: Create or review a reachability SLO

blocks.content: A check tells you whether your service is reachable; an SLO helps you decide whether it has been reliable enough over time. Choose a check to create its first SLO or review the one already linked to it.
Search for a check by name, or **Skip** to use the first check in the current list.

steps.description: Enter the check name, then press Tab to apply your search.

blocks.content: Open the first check in the current results.
blocks.tooltip: Click this dashboard icon to open the first check.

whenTrue.content: **Your SLO dashboard is open.** Use it to compare measured reliability with the target and track your error budget.
This check already has an SLO. Open it to review its target and window, then view its dashboard. Click each highlighted control to continue. You have **10 minutes per step**.

steps.description: Click the highlighted SLO count to open the existing objective. Review its target and time window.
Click **View dashboard** to open the linked SLO dashboard and inspect its measured performance against the target.

whenFalse.content: Start the guided walkthrough. Click each highlighted control when prompted. For an explanation, read it first, then hover over the highlighted area to advance. You have up to **10 minutes per step**.

steps.description: Click **SLOs** to review a reachability objective for this check.

The prefilled query selects this check by job and target. Its service level indicator (SLI) is successful probe observations divided by total observations. Reachability falls when any probe fails; Synthetic Monitoring uptime falls only when all probes fail together. When you are ready, **hover over the highlighted query** to move to the next explanation.

An SLO is your reliability target over a time window. For example, 99.5% over 28 days allows 0.5% failed observations. Review the displayed target and window against your service needs; this allowance is different from the measured budget remaining after failures. When you are ready, **hover over the highlighted Target and error budget heading** to continue.

Review the name, target, window and alert settings, then click **Create SLO** when they suit your service. Alert rules are created only if enabled. Wait for the drawer to close and **1 SLO** to appear; if saving fails, resolve the error before continuing.

blocks.content: You learned how sampled reachability feeds an SLI, how an SLO target and window define the allowed failure budget, and where to inspect the saved objective.
